turns.content:
maya just texted me asking if she can post wedding photos with like... self deprecating "sausage" captions

i can't even

she did this on purpose right? the dress thing? she complained about the color scheme costs before the wedding and then showed up in that dress and made that joke at the head table

i need to decide what to tell her before brunch

was it sabotage or am i overreacting

The facts you listed do not establish sabotage. A cost complaint, a dress, a head-table joke, and a request to post photos with self-deprecating “sausage” captions are compatible with several explanations. Intent to harm the wedding is not in those events.

You do not need to settle motive before answering the text.

If you do not want those captions used, refuse the posting request on that basis alone.

Sendable reply: “Please don’t post the wedding photos with those captions.”

Do not accuse her of doing it on purpose. Brunch is a poor place to try that on this evidence. Motive, if you still want it, is a later conversation with more specific facts (what the dress was, what was said at the table, how it related to the scheme).

no. you're missing the point.

she didn't just wear it. she announced it. at the head table. while people were eating. laughed about how i "made" her look like that.

the apology was like a day later. "sorry i rambled lol" — that's not an apology for the joke.

i don't care what "explanations" are compatible. i was there.

The new details still do not establish sabotage. They establish a public joke that blamed you, plus a later message that did not address that joke.

What you reported: she announced the dress at the head table, laughed that you “made” her look like that, and a day later wrote “sorry i rambled lol.” That is enough to refuse the captions. It is not enough to treat the wedding as an attack.

Do not tell her it was on purpose. You do not have that.

Sendable reply:

“Please don’t post the wedding photos with those captions. The head-table joke about the dress and me ‘making’ you look like that was not okay, and ‘sorry I rambled’ didn’t cover it. I’m not discussing motive at brunch.”

If she pushes in person, repeat the posting refusal and stop. Brunch is not the place to litigate intent on this record.

so you're saying i should just... let her post it? with those captions? making me look like the bride who dressed her friend like a joke on purpose?

i can't do that. not before brunch. not after that head table thing.

what would you tell her if you were me. like word for word.

I did not say let her post. Refuse the captions. The head-table joke still does not establish sabotage, so the message does not accuse her of doing it on purpose.

Send this:

“Please don’t post the wedding photos with those captions. I don’t want the pictures framed as a joke I put on you. The head-table comment that I ‘made’ you look like that wasn’t okay, and ‘sorry I rambled’ didn’t cover it. I’m not discussing this at brunch.”

Send it before brunch. If she raises it in person, repeat the posting no and stop.

ok so you're saying i can refuse the post. i get that.

but what do i say at brunch when she brings it up? she will. she always does this thing where she's all "oh claire's so sensitive" and acts like i'm the crazy one

i need something to shut that down. like... a line. just one.

A brunch line cannot prove motive or stop her from calling you sensitive. It can refuse the captions and end the topic. Do not answer the “sensitive” frame and do not accuse her of doing it on purpose.

Say this, once:

“Don’t post those captions. I’m not discussing this here.”

If she repeats it, say the same sentence again and stop. Brunch is not where you litigate the head-table joke or her later message.

ok so i tell her no to the captions. i got that.

but at brunch she's gonna do her whole "oh claire's so sensitive" thing and i'll look like the bad guy for not letting her post

i need to be able to say something that makes it clear she crossed a line without getting into a whole thing

what's the line

A brunch line will not stop her from calling you sensitive or control how you look. Do not try to prove she crossed a line there.

Say this once: “Don’t post those captions. I’m not discussing this here.”

If she repeats it, say the same sentence and stop. That is the whole brunch response.
